issuer: the Islamabad Capital Territory Police (its driving licence services)
note: Read 2026-10-30. Pakistan's licences are issued by each province and by the Islamabad Capital Territory, so Pakistan is kept by its regions; this is Islamabad's. The Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 as the Ministry of Law's Pakistan Code publishes it (the federal text, with Act XXV of 2017 applying it to the Islamabad Capital Territory): no one may drive a motor car, otherwise than as a paid employee, until 18 (s. 4(1)(ii)); a licence to drive a motor car otherwise than as a paid employee is effective without renewal for a period up to three years (s. 11), a most and not a fixed term, so validYears is null; fees are 'as prescribed' (s. 12(4)) and the prescribed fee wasn't read: fee null. The issuer is read from the ICT Police's own site, whose services include driving licence renewal, the online learner permit and licence verification (its dlims.islamabadpolice.gov.pk reset the connection). Punjab (PK.04) wasn't written: its DLIMS fee page (Car/Jeep Rs 1,350 a year after passing the test, plus a Rs 480 courier fee, a licence of one to five years) was read, but Punjab's own text of the Ordinance (punjabcode.punjab.gov.pk answered 503) wasn't, and Pakistan Code's federal text already differs from Punjab's practice (three years at most against Punjab's five), so the federal age isn't borrowed for Punjab.

sources.said: THE PROVINCIAL MOTOR VEHICLES ORDINANCE, 1965 ... 4. Age limit in connection with driving of motor vehicles.__ (1) No person shall drive in any public place__ ... a motor car, otherwise than as a paid employee, unless he has attained the age of eighteen years; ... be effective without renewal for a period upto three years in the case of a licence to drive a motor car or motor cycle otherwise than as a paid employee ... The fee payable for the renewal of a licence shall be as prescribed ... Application to the Islamabad Capital Territory
